channel.title: Tottertop Journal
channel.description: Development notes on Tottertop — what the game is and why we are making it.

item.title: One tap per block: how Tottertop is played
item.description: One tap decides when a block lets go. Where it lands is up to the tower and the wobble.

item.title: A short game on purpose: why a round takes about a minute
item.description: A bus stop, a few minutes before a meeting. Short is a design choice, and we also write down its limits.

item.title: The first round, and a reason for one more
item.description: Tips that never pause the game, a “New best!” that appears mid-round, and a single goal for the next try.

item.title: Telling the blocks apart: a color-blind check
item.description: In a simulation of green color blindness, the blue and purple blocks were nearly identical. How a contrast test caught it, and the rule every block color set now has to pass.

item.title: iPhone first, and what iCloud sync does
item.description: iPhone only at first, and progress that follows you between phones. What syncs and what does not.

item.title: Why Tottertop is meant to be free, with no ads
item.description: No ads and nothing to buy. What a fully free rule changes in how the game is built.

item.title: Why this journal posts once a day
item.description: One post a day, in twelve languages, written about things that actually happened. A note on how this journal works and what it will not do.

item.title: What we test before anything ships
item.description: Nearly 700 automated tests, a layout check in every language, and bot players. And the list of things no test can settle.

item.title: Sound switched on, nothing heard: the iPhone silent switch
item.description: The setting was on, the code path was fine, and the game was still silent. The cause was one audio mode that obeys the silent switch.

item.title: Twelve languages, one fixed order
item.description: Our first post said eleven languages. It is twelve now, in a fixed order, with a language picker and a test that makes every one fit a 320 px screen.

item.title: The “Perfect” that was not: three fixes from day one
item.description: A “Perfect” on a block that topples the tower, a first block that fell on floor one, a best score lost mid-collapse: three bugs from one evening.

item.title: One tower for everyone: how the daily seed works
item.description: A daily tower only works if everyone really gets the same one. How we turn a date into a block order that is identical on every phone in the world.

item.title: Tuning the wobble with bots instead of hands
item.description: Before a human could play Tottertop, we tuned its difficulty with three bots of different skill, 200 rounds each. What the numbers said, and what they cannot say.

item.title: Why we moved from a dark night sky to mint and sky
item.description: Two days after the dark night-sky look, a polish pass changed almost nothing you could see. So we redrew the whole game bright, round and cute.

item.title: What Tottertop is, and why we are making it
item.description: What Tottertop is — a one-tap physics stacker where a crane drops blocks onto a wobbling tower — and why ipe() wants to make a game this small.
